item.text:
**8B.3 Research Note**

**Positive / partial evidence**
- **Title:** Govt adopts plan to turn public welfare services into smart services in two years  
  **Publisher:** UNB  
  **Date:** June 4, 2024  
  **URL:** https://unb.com.bd/category/Bangladesh/govt-adopts-plan-to-turn-public-welfare-services-into-smart-services-in-two-years/136812  
  **Claim:** The government brought 52 ministries and divisions into the Smart Bangladesh implementation platform and told them to convert public welfare services into smart services within two years. This is concrete whole-of-government mobilization, not just slogan use.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Official Document: Govt to include Smart Bangladesh in mid-term dev plan  
  **Publisher:** Dhaka Tribune  
  **Date:** April 16, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/344095/official-document-govt-to-include-smart  
  **Claim:** Planning authorities sought to embed Smart Bangladesh into the Ninth Five Year Plan, with goals including upper-middle-income status, macro stability, jobs, poverty reduction, and rule of law. This shows the program being translated into planning architecture.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Title:** Sheikh Hasina sworn in as PM for 5th term, forms 37-member cabinet  
  **Publisher:** BSS  
  **Date:** January 11, 2024  
  **URL:** https://b.bssnews.net/news-flash/167551  
  **Claim:** Hasina formed a 37-member cabinet that included two technocrats, Yeafesh Osman and Samanta Lal Sen. That is limited but real evidence of staffing the government with some non-party specialists.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** e-GP to be made mandatory in public procurement as part of reforms  
  **Publisher:** BPPA  
  **Date:** March 6, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1483.html  
  **Claim:** BPPA said the government was making e-GP mandatory in procurement, moving toward full digitization, and handling contract management through the platform. That is concrete administrative enforcement of reform.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Title:** IMF Executive Board Concludes the Second Review under Bangladesh’s ECF/EFF/RSF  
  **Publisher:** IMF  
  **Date:** June 24, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/24/pr24234-bangladesh-imf-exec-board-concludes-2nd-review-ecf-eff-rsf  
  **Claim:** The IMF said program performance was broadly on track and cited exchange-rate realignment, a crawling peg, tighter monetary policy, tax/subsidy reform, and continued policy actions. This is the strongest evidence that the government could execute at least some macro reforms under pressure.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Title:** Bangladesh Receives $900 million World Bank Financing to Increase Economic and Urban Resilience  
  **Publisher:** World Bank  
  **Date:** June 21, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/21/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-increase-economic-and-urban-resilience-for-sustainable-growth  
  **Claim:** The package supported fiscal and financial-sector reforms, stronger banking oversight, institutionalization of e-GP, and resilience spending. This is direct evidence of translating a policy agenda into instruments and institutions.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Advancing healthcare excellence: WHO’s role in developing the first national medical education strategy in Bangladesh  
  **Publisher:** WHO Bangladesh  
  **Date:** March 4, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh  
  **Claim:** The health ministry, with WHO support, used workforce studies and a technical working group to build a medical-education strategy. That shows some evidence-based bureaucracy and follow-through inside a sector ministry.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** 2nd JEE Bangladesh  
  **Publisher:** WHO  
  **Date:** July 11, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.who.int/southeastasia/news/detail/11-07-2024-2nd-jee-bn  
  **Claim:** Bangladesh completed a peer-reviewed Joint External Evaluation that identified strengths, gaps, and priority actions. This is a real measurement-and-correction mechanism inside the state apparatus.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2

**Negative evidence**
- **Title:** Bangladesh PM Hasina secures fourth straight term in vote boycotted by main opposition  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint  
  **Date:** January 8, 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-pm-sheikh-hasina-secures-fourth-straight-term-in-vote-boycotted-by-main-opposition/1914659/  
  **Claim:** Reuters said the BNP boycotted the vote after Hasina refused to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election. That indicates she used the electoral apparatus for regime survival rather than neutral contestation.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Title:** New Cabinet Formation: Loyalists, fresh faces likely to get priority  
  **Publisher:** The Daily Star  
  **Date:** January 9, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/new-cabinet-formation-loyalists-fresh-faces-likely-get-priority-3515421  
  **Claim:** Contemporaneous reporting said Hasina would likely rely on party loyalists, with technocrats expected to be rare. That points to patronage-leaning mobilization of the executive rather than broad technocratic deployment.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh blocks roads and internet, deploys army to curb protests  
  **Publisher:** Reuters  
  **Date:** July 20, 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/  
  **Claim:** Reuters reported soldiers, roadblocks, curfews, and internet/text shutdowns used against protesters. This is strong evidence of state apparatus mobilized for coercive regime defense, not just program execution.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2, 1B.8

- **Title:** Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain  
  **Publisher:** Reuters  
  **Date:** July 22, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153  
  **Claim:** Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence. That supports a reading of coercive control and blame-shifting rather than effective state coordination for a stated public program.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Exclusive: Bangladesh army refused to suppress protest, sealing Hasina’s fate  
  **Publisher:** Reuters  
  **Date:** August 7, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.voanews.com/a/exclusive-bangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasina-s-fate/7733166.html  
  **Claim:** Reuters reported the army decided not to fire on civilians to enforce Hasina’s curfew. That is strong counterevidence on effective mobilization: she sought coercive support, but the military would not fully carry it out.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh’s internet shutdown isolates citizens, disrupts business  
  **Publisher:** Reuters  
  **Date:** July 26, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladeshs-internet-shutdown-isolates-citizens-disrupts-business-3539448  
  **Claim:** Reuters described a countrywide internet blackout used during the unrest, with similar controls used previously around elections. This shows blunt enforcement capacity, but aimed at information suppression and regime security.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Al govt created lawless economy; crony capitalism captured public organizations  
  **Publisher:** The Daily Star  
  **Date:** October 31, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/al-govt-created-lawless-economy-3741796  
  **Claim:** A white-paper lead said authoritarian practices produced crony capitalism and a nexus of politicians, bureaucrats, and business interests that captured public organizations. That is strong evidence the ruling network was mobilized for patronage and capture, not clean execution.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.3, 8B.2

**Bottom line**
- **Best positive case:** Hasina did translate parts of the program into real machinery, especially Smart Bangladesh planning, e-GP procurement, IMF/World Bank-backed macro reforms, and some sectoral technical work.
- **Best negative case:** Her biggest mobilization success in 2024 was coercive regime defense, not program execution. The July crackdown, internet shutdowns, and reliance on the army show the apparatus was used effectively for control, but not in a stable or rights-respecting way.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a single 2024 source that ties the whole program to a full budget annex, KPI dashboard, or government-wide implementation calendar with durable results. The strongest positives are sectoral and procedural; the strongest negatives are coercive and crisis-driven.
